models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign, light-air pattern over the Aeolians - useful context, but far too early to call the trip dates.
briefing.synopsis: Current sampled consensus across all available models shows a slack pressure pattern with no organised gradient: winds at all six islands running 1-7 kt through 30 Sep-2 Oct, swinging between E/NE overnight and N/NNW by afternoon, with seas at 0.1-0.4 ft. ECMWF IFS 0.25° and AIFS (both 30 Sep 06Z) and ICON-2i (30 Sep 12Z) all keep it in that range; the only flagged spread is Portorosa at 00:00 on 1 Oct, where the models disagree across 0.2-7.7 kt. The guidance horizon runs to 23:00 on 6 Oct, so the first three trip days are only just entering range and the later legs are not covered at all.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: No fleet afloat tonight - this is a pre-trip outlook. For the pre-departure night of 3 Oct at Portorosa, IFS 0.25° (30 Sep 06Z) gives 2.5 kt ESE, gusting 6.4, with 0.1 ft swell from the NW; the enclosed marina is the recommended and only listed berth, and offers all-round shelter regardless. Nothing in the payload suggests a reason to look elsewhere, but the picture will be re-run before you arrive.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: For the trip itself, the computed guidance favours an 06:00 start on every leg currently in range, with Portorosa to Lipari on 4 Oct showing 5.5 kt SSE, gusts 11.5, and 0.1 ft seas in the 06:00 window (IFS 0.25°/AIFS, 30 Sep 06Z). Wind falls to 2 kt or less by mid-morning on several days, so expect motoring rather than a weather problem. Treat all of this as pattern information only - at 72-120 h lead, run-to-run direction changes have averaged 59 degrees across 23 compared snapshots.

passage_notes.note: Go at this range: 06:00 window 5.5 kt SSE, gusts 11.5, seas 0.1 ft - a run on 179 TWA. Wind drops to 2-4 kt after 10:00.
1.4-3.5 kt E backing N through the day, seas 0.1 ft. Effectively a motoring leg; the 10:00 window is head-to-wind.
2-5 kt NE to N, gusts to 8.7, seas 0.1 ft. Long light-air leg - budget engine hours.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (6 Oct, 11 nm)
passage_notes.note: 3.5-4.7 kt NNE all day, gusts to 10.5, seas 0.2-0.3 ft. A run in either window.

passage_notes.leg: Panarea → Filicudi and Filicudi → Salina (7-8 Oct)
passage_notes.note: Beyond the 6 Oct forecast horizon - no trip-date guidance yet. Only a rehearsal run against this week's live weather exists, which is not a forecast.

cautions: The trip dates from 7 Oct onward are outside the guidance horizon entirely - nothing in this briefing applies to them.

Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli is scored only 'workable' and is open from every direction, with no anchoring permitted; shelter there depends entirely on it staying calm, so it needs a fresh look the morning of any Stromboli night.
Gust figures of 8-12 kt against 1-4 kt means recur throughout. These are interval-maximum values from IFS 0.25° in very light air, reported but not treated as a caution.
Portorosa, 00:00 on 1 Oct: models disagree across 0.2-7.7 kt - no usable consensus for that hour.
The 'go' verdicts in the payload are conservative threshold checks against light-air numbers, not a decision. The skipper's call on the morning stands.
briefing.confidence_note: IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree closely on a light-air, flat-sea pattern and run-to-run wind-speed shifts have been small (mean 0.9 kt at 72-120 h), but mean direction shifts of 59 degrees at that lead and a horizon ending 6 Oct mean the trip dates themselves are not yet forecastable.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
